identity.title: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics

problem.claim: Evaluate general-purpose mobile GUI agents under diverse, unstable, user-centric conditions resembling real mobile use.

gap.claim: Existing online benchmarks are app-centric and task-homogeneous, while coarse evaluation obscures fine-grained failure causes such as perception and memory deficiencies.

contributions.claim: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark with user-intent-driven task design for realistic mobile usage.
Adds capability-oriented annotations for fine-grained analysis of agent behavior and failures.
Provides code and data for the benchmark.

stated_novelty.claim: The benchmark combines user-centric task definition with capability-oriented evaluation, addressing both what and how to evaluate for mobile GUI agents.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that state-of-the-art agents show large performance gaps relative to prior benchmarks, which they interpret as evidence that the tasks are more challenging and realistic.
Authors report that diagnostic analysis attributes most failures to perception and memory deficiencies.
Authors report near-zero success for even the strongest agents under environment variations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing benchmarks do not capture the diversity and instability of real mobile usage.
VenusBench-Mobile evaluates realistic user-centric tasks and annotates capabilities for fine-grained diagnosis.
Reported results show substantially larger performance gaps than prior benchmarks and near-zero success under environment variation.
Failures are reported as dominated by perception and memory deficits; the benchmark is positioned as a step toward robust deployment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns benchmark construction with a diagnostic annotation scheme, then reports both aggregate performance gaps and capability-specific failure patterns.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing realistic evaluation with structured diagnosis can make poor performance more actionable than a single success metric.
lessons.application: When introducing a benchmark, define task realism and failure-capability labels together, and report aggregate results alongside diagnostic breakdowns.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when reliable capability labels are unavailable or the task has no meaningful decomposition.

unknowns: The abstract gives no dataset size, task distribution, metrics, numerical performance values, or details of environment variations.
It does not specify the evaluated agents, annotation procedure, or whether the reported diagnoses were independently validated.
